A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same work, Less Greedy Equivalence Search, with complete main text and Appendices A–E. Text, equations, pseudocode, tables, and figures support reliable comparison, including content moved or renamed between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations measuring causal-graph recovery and runtime, experiments with misspecified prior assumptions and interventions, and analyses of the Sachs protein-signaling dataset.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulation and Sachs results and reports additional comparisons involving XGES and expanded less-greedy algorithm variants.

M1.justification: Beyond carrying the original LGES design into LGES-0, v2 introduces deletion/turning priority in LGES and forced-deletion restarts in LGES+ (Algorithms 1, 8–9). GGES accommodates mixed operator schedules. v1's LGIES meant LGES followed by I-ORIENT; v2 retains that pipeline separately and introduces LGIES variants that incorporate less-greedy insertion directly into GIES.

E1.justification: v2 adds the sparser ER1 observational setting and extends interventional evaluation to ER3 graphs (Section D.1.4 and Figure 5). Observational learning, misspecified prior knowledge, interventional learning, and continuous/discretized Sachs data remain the same core tasks and domains.

E2.justification: XGES-0 and XGES become evaluated comparators in Section 5.1 and Figure 4b; their source paper was cited but these methods were not evaluated in v1. Comparisons also expand to the new LGES+ and interventional variants, while retaining GES, PC, NoTears, and GIES in the relevant experiments.

E3.justification: Within the retained simulation framework, v2's reported small-sample evaluation drops n = 500, and its scalability evaluation stops at 250 rather than including 500 variables. Example 2 changes from 1,000 to 100 samples per dataset. These revise specific settings; the principal data-generation procedure, accuracy measures, and 50-dataset design remain.

E4.justification: Figure 4b adds a systematic comparison testing whether less-greedy insertion helps across GES, XGES-0, XGES, and GIES. Density sensitivity is extended to ER1. Conversely, v1's scoring-operation analyses and detailed ER3 error and classification breakdowns disappear; the prior-misspecification analysis remains, reorganized.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly defines plotted error bars as one standard deviation across 50 random seeds. v2 retains error bars and reports 50 simulated datasets but removes their statistical definition from the captions. Its remaining table still reports mean ± standard deviation. This is a reporting loss, not evidence that retained experiments used fewer runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive results for XGES and the new less-greedy variants. Table D.1.1 retains v1's 175-variable conservative LGES SHD of 42.04 ± 11.51 as LGES-0 and adds 39.457 ± 10.44 for the modified LGES. Example 2 changes from 69%/31% to 96%/4% under a changed sample size. Results for 500-variable graphs and several detailed metric breakdowns are removed; Sachs outcomes remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C extends Theorem 1's argument beyond the original forward/backward procedure to turning and mixed insertion/deletion schedules. It supplies correctness arguments for the newly defined LGES and LGES+ variants, while carrying the original LGES argument into Corollary C.1 for LGES-0. The SAFEINSERT and I-ORIENT results are largely retained.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contribution on LGES and its I-ORIENT extension. v2's conclusion presents a family of less-greedy algorithms and claims that the insertion strategies improve existing GES-style searches more broadly. The retained speed, accuracy, and robustness claims therefore acquire a substantially broader algorithmic scope.

C2.justification: New Section B.1 explains why analogous filtering of deletions could preserve false adjacencies, how LGES searches fewer separating sets than PC, and why DAG selection warrants further study. Section 5.3 distinguishes the guarantees of SAFEINSERT plus I-ORIENT from the empirical advantages of LGIES. Existing causal-sufficiency and faithfulness limitations largely remain.

D1.justification: v2 identifies and supplies pseudocode for the implemented CPDAG-to-DAG selection procedure (Algorithm 7). It also documents the common Python implementation used for GES-family comparisons and exclusion of optimized XGES operators. These improve implementation disclosure; hardware, principal baseline parameters, and the stated project-code location remain unchanged.

R1.justification: XGES shifts from a supporting citation to an explicit methodological predecessor whose heuristics are incorporated and compared against (Section 3.4). Section A.2.2 expands the distinction between perfect and misspecified background knowledge, including Knowledge-Guided GES. Additional references support prior-based scoring, DAG conversion/sampling, and discussion of hidden-variable settings.

P1.justification: Several method and experiment sections are substantially rewritten. Section 3.3 separates initialization from guided search, Section 4 adds a structured explanation of orientation, and Appendix B is divided into design, limitations, and examples. Algorithm naming, contribution framing, and the terminology of model repairing versus prior knowledge are revised throughout.

P2.justification: The empirical displays are extensively redesigned. Figure 4 adds grouped cross-family comparisons; Figure 5 becomes a multi-panel accuracy/runtime comparison across densities. Appendix figures reorganize comparator groups, the small-sample heatmaps and accompanying table are replaced by line plots, and the large-graph table changes rows and metric structure. Explanatory graph diagrams are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses an important gap in v1: XGES was cited but not evaluated. Direct XGES/XGES-0 comparisons and paired insertion-strategy tests across algorithm families substantially strengthen validation of the central idea. Extended correctness arguments and implementation explanations make the broader contribution more assessable. Removed stress-test results, undefined plotted error bars, and stale FAQ references to omitted settings weaken reporting, but do not outweigh the central validation gains.
